 PS5 Jailbreak App "Overdrive" Allegedly Offers Free Games and DLC 
 Updated 
 by DrUsmanSaleem 
 Oct 12th, 2026 15:00
 Discuss (14 Comments) 
 A new app called Overdrive is making the rounds on X , and apparently it is a free game store for jailbroken PS5 consoles. Insider Gaming reports that a clip was posted on October 11 by Edigax on X, showing an app that works like the PlayStation Store but offers games and DLC at no cost. The listings show download size and a review score instead of prices, with titles like Battlefield 6 and Forza Horizon 5 reportedly in the library. We don't know who made Overdrive, where the files come from, or whether it works as smoothly as the video suggests, so take this with a pinch of salt. Initial accounts have been mixed, with one Redditor describing the app as "very poorly made."
It isn't the only such app. Orbit Store , an open-source beta from developer saawant12, offers a similar storefront with 147 games linked from Archive.org, though its developer says Orbit doesn't host any files itself. Both arrive shortly after Relapse, a public jailbreak for PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles on firmware 7.00 through 13.60. The homebrew scene has been busy since, with PS2 discs now loading and Halo 2 reportedly hitting 30 FPS via an Xbox emulator. Sony has been actively pushing back against the jailbreak, releasing firmware 14.00 that sits outside Relapse's range, and the October 1 update (14.10) added more security fixes. With no official downgrade path, updating currently means losing the jailbreak. As for Overdrive, readers are advised to stay away from this app. Jailbreaking voids the warranty and can get a PSN account banned, and running unsigned apps from unknown sources is an easy way to invite malware or brick the console. Downloading paid games this way is, of course, piracy, which TechPowerUp does not condone. Sony hasn't commented yet, though it's reasonable to expect the company to squash Overdrive quickly, probably with another firmware update.
 Update Oct 14th : Sony Interactive Entertainment has reportedly sent the developers of Overdrive a cease-and-desist letter, effectively shutting down the app.
